excl.s: Heavy AI spending has pushed Alphabet, Amazon and Meta into negative free cash flow; Ramp data shows Google trailing in business agentic AI usage and Delaware leading states in AI adoption at about 73%.
Big Tech earnings and Anthropic's mid-November IPO will test investor appetite for AI; Ramp data shows a record 8% of firms switched AI providers in September.
New Ramp data shows AI spend growth slowed sharply over the past two months; Ramp's economist points to falling prices for frontier models.

items.t: With a weak board and no successor, Nvidia confronts a governance crisis
items.s: Huang's admitted affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset knocked roughly 5% and over $200 billion off Nvidia's value, exposing a long-tenured board and no clear No. 2 or successor.

items.t: AI chip financing hits a wall
items.s: Lenders are dumping data-center and GPU loans at steep discounts on fears the debt outlives the hardware, with ING shopping $500 million of loans and Ares saying it will avoid GPU financing.

items.t: New White House chief of staff Miller shuts door on big business
items.s: Stephen Miller's replacement of Susie Wiles ends the access CEOs relied on to soften administration policy, setting up more direct clashes with business.

items.t: PepsiCo to cut about 1,000 jobs as North American business struggles
items.s: PepsiCo is eliminating roughly 1,000 positions as its North American unit continues to underperform.

items.t: Boeing to cut 5% of commercial airplane unit as product ramp-up delayed
items.s: Boeing plans to trim about 5% of its commercial airplanes workforce after delays in ramping up production of its jets.

items.t: CoreWeave confronts 'doom cycle' as neocloud credit risk overshadows growth
items.s: Concerns about debt and credit risk at AI neocloud providers are overshadowing CoreWeave's revenue growth.

items.t: The U.S. will hit its debt limit sooner than expected
items.s: Projections show the federal government reaching its borrowing cap earlier than forecast, with the default deadline potentially landing while Congress is on recess.

items.t: Anthropic debuts Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models, undercutting OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra on price
items.s: Ahead of its IPO, Anthropic released updated frontier models priced well below OpenAI's comparable offering.

items.t: So long, Cybertruck
items.s: Tesla is winding down Cybertruck production and refunding many buyers' deposits as it shifts focus to its autonomous Cybercab.
Nvidia's board has opened a probe into Huang's ties to a person accused of spying for China, and lawmakers are taking a closer look as well.
items.t: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with alleged Chinese spy

items.s: Employers are using AI to fill roles faster, which is cutting into what staffing and recruiting firms can charge.
items.t: AI is speeding up recruitment — and putting agency fees under pressure

items.s: Building U.S. reserves of tungsten, rare earths and other critical minerals at Cold War scale is proving difficult given limited supply outside China.
items.t: Pentagon's war stockpile plan hits a critical minerals wall

items.s: An economist argues last week's AI-led stock rout also revealed growing investor demand for a risk premium on Treasury debt.
items.t: The market selloff exposed Wall Street's true fears about U.S. debt, top economist warns

items.s: Holiday flight prices are at their highest in a decade, so sale fares may just bring travelers back to 2025 levels.
items.t: Holiday airfares hit a 10-year high, and Black Friday deals may only match last year's prices

items.s: Meta's longtime finance executive is departing to become chief financial officer of AI inference startup Fireworks.
items.t: Meta top exec Dave Wehner leaves to join AI startup Fireworks as CFO

items.s: Anthropic's planned listing arrives just as voters signaled opposition to data center expansion, complicating the pitch to public investors.
items.t: Anthropic IPO meets AI backlash after midterms show stinging rebuke of data centers

items.s: Solo-owner business formation is running strong, with founders leaning on AI tools to do work that once required staff.
items.t: America's new small businesses with no employees are off to hot start in AI era

items.s: Bank executives are preparing for more political scrutiny after the midterms but few foresee major rule changes soon.
items.t: Wall Street banks expect little regulatory change as Democrats return to power

items.s: Oil companies are already developing the lithium-rich Smackover brine deposits, which could reshape the domestic battery supply chain.
items.t: Arkansas' Smackover formation could cut U.S. reliance on Chinese lithium

items.s: October payrolls nearly tripled forecasts and unemployment dipped to 4.1%, though long-term joblessness rose to its highest since 2021.
items.t: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, way more than expected; unemployment rate slips to 4.1%

items.s: Microsoft is consolidating its relationships with third-party AI cloud providers as the data-center buildout comes under pressure.
items.t: Microsoft plans to use fewer neoclouds as AI buildout shows signs of strain

items.s: After midterm voters backed local data-center restrictions, OpenAI promised to cover its own electricity costs and post guarantees to win community support.
items.t: OpenAI pledges to pay its own power costs and post financial guarantees after voters push back on data centers

items.s: JPMorgan's dealmaking head sees M&A activity cooling next year, with private-equity exits and refinancing deadlines as a potential offset.
items.t: JPMorgan's M&A chief expects a softer 2027, with possible upside from private equity exits

items.s: Exchanges want GPU compute to trade like a commodity, but national-security concerns in Washington could complicate the plan.
items.t: Wall Street's push to trade AI compute hits Washington roadblock

items.s: A French bank reported €100 million stolen in a wave of cyberattacks that also struck a blood bank and supermarket refrigeration systems.
items.t: A series of cyber attacks rattles France

items.s: McDonald's CEO is betting on risk-taking, accountability and chicken to restart U.S. sales growth.
items.t: Chris Kempczinski's new value menu for McDonald's

items.s: Nasdaq and S&P 500 bounced Friday led by Nvidia, but both remained on pace for their worst week since June after the post-midterm AI rout.
items.t: Stocks rebound after tech selloff that pushed Nasdaq into correction

items.s: HP has named Walmsley as its new chief executive, the latest in a busy stretch of corporate leadership changes.
items.t: Walmsley takes HP's top job as the CEO revolving door turns

items.s: A sharp drop in US tech stocks wiped out the rally that followed the midterm elections.
items.t: US tech selloff erases post-midterm gains

items.s: Election-outcome betting platforms emerged as big winners from the US midterms, drawing heavy activity and attention.
items.t: Prediction markets win big on election night

items.s: Voters in more than 30 localities across nine states approved bans, moratoriums and other limits on data centers, a setback for the AI infrastructure buildout.
items.t: US voters roundly reject data centers in ballot measures
